notes:
Account overview:
- Enterprise trading analytics vendor exploring LLM augmentation for trader desk assistants and document reranking. Sensitive PII + market data — strict EU residency.

Engagement stage / ask:
- 2-week evaluation POC focused on latency SLO alignment and reserved GPU sizing. Primary ask: clear definitions for p50/p95/p99 across streaming and non-streaming flows and a reproducible measurement plan.

Key technical requirements (from calls):
- Workloads: short-form chat + single-turn reranking + periodic embeddings reindex. Peak expected QPS ~ 350-500 req/s during trading hours. Sustained throughput requirement for dedicated pool of ~400 req/s.
- Latency targets (Saffron initial): non-streaming single-turn: p50 <= 40ms, p95 <= 120ms, p99 <= 250ms. Streaming chat: TTFB (time-to-first-byte) p50 <= 30ms, TTE (time-to-end) p95 <= 300ms for < 512-token responses.
- Cost sensitivity: prefer reserved capacity pricing with burst pockets; exploring 6-8 A100-equivalent GPUs reserved initially.

Measurement alignment discussion notes:
- Terminology alignment: client-side vs server-side timings clarified on call. Saffron insists on client-side numbers in SLA but accepts server-side canonical telemetry for debugging. We proposed: canonical SLA = server-side "response_ready" to "token_emitted" plus network median; contractual measurement = synthetic client-side probes from EU egress points run by Redwood with signed traces.
- Measurement points to capture: client_send_ts, server_recv_ts, server_resp_start_ts, token_emit_ts(s), client_receive_last_token_ts. Use monotonic clocks and correlate via trace-id.
- Percentile semantics: agree p99 understood as the 99th percentile of the distribution of end-to-end completed-request durations measured over sliding 1-hour windows; not bucketed per-second. For streaming, compute separate percentiles for TTFB and TTE.
- Streaming specifics: define two SLA metrics: TTFB (time to first token) and TTR (time to requested token rate stability). Also account for partial responses — SLA measured only on completed responses unless explicitly marked as long-poll.
- Warm vs cold start: exclude first N minutes after model load or deployment rollback from SLA windows. Define warm-up window = 5 minutes after model swap; cache-priming expected in POC.
- Batching & concurrency: Saffron will require transparency on effective batch sizes and queue delay. We proposed maximum queue_delay SLA clause: 95th percentile queue delay <= 30ms under target throughput.

POC plan (2 weeks):
- Week 1: baseline telemetry & synthetic client probes from 3 EU vantage points; run hosted Redwood dedicated cluster with 4xA100 equivalent GPUs; compare model-v1 (fp16) vs quantized variants.
- Week 2: scale to 8x GPUs reserved, run mixed workload (chat + rerank), collect p50/p95/p99 TTFB/TTE, measure throughput headroom, run failure scenarios (node preemption, network spike).
- Deliverables: measurement workbook (CSV/BigQuery table stub), SLA draft with definitions, sizing recommendation and cost/benefit tradeoffs, runbook for fallbacks (model variant routing, cross-region failover).

SLA negotiation points flagged by Saffron legal:
- Contractual measurement authority: Redwood vs third-party probe vendor. Saffron prefers third-party endorsed probes.
- Remedies: credits vs guaranteed minimal throughput. They asked for clear overage/noise allowances during market open spikes.

Action items (who/when):
- Diego: produce POC telemetry template + tracing instrumentation checklist by 2026-02-05.
- Maya: prepare draft SLA clauses for latency percentiles, measurement method, warm-up exclusions by 2026-02-12.
- Security: share SOC2 Type II and EU data residency architecture diagram (link above).

Quotes & shorthand from calls:
- "We need p99s to not tank during open — traders will walk away if tail latency spikes." — Head of Platform, Saffron.
- "Client-side numbers are what our ops runbooks alert on; we need Redwood to help make those reproducible."

Open technical blockers:
- Trace propagation across customer frontend -> Redwood ingress not instrumented; need SDK snippet.
- Legal redline around "data residency" language in SOW.
- Capacity procurement lead time: 4-6 weeks for reserved GPU commit approvals.

Next steps summary:
- Finalize measurement definitions (canonical server-side vs contractual client-side) + agree on probe topology.
- Lock reserved GPU sizing after POC (target decision meeting 2026-03-15).
- Run security review and provide SOC2 artifacts.
